listening.title: How plants spread their seeds
listening.contextDescription: A lecture in an introductory botany course on the ways in which plants disperse their seeds.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Today's topic is seed dispersal: in other words, how plants manage to move their seeds away from the parent plant. Unlike animals, plants can't walk away to find new places to live, so the seed is really their only chance to travel. And it's important that seeds do travel, because a seedling that grows right next to its parent has to compete with it for light, water and nutrients, and it's also more likely to be attacked by pests and diseases that have built up around the older plant.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Plants have developed a remarkable range of ways of spreading their seeds, and we can group them into four main methods: wind, water, animals and what we might call self-dispersal.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Let's begin with wind. Seeds that are carried by the wind are usually small and light, and many have special structures that help them stay in the air for longer. The dandelion is a good example. Each seed is attached to a tiny umbrella of fine hairs, which acts like a parachute, and research has shown that these seeds can travel very long distances in the right conditions. Maple trees take a different approach. Their seeds have a single wing, and as they fall they spin like the blades of a helicopter. This spinning slows their fall, which gives the wind more time to carry them away from the tree. Orchids go to the extreme: their seeds are so small that they're almost like dust.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: The second method is water. Plants that live by rivers, lakes or the sea often produce seeds or fruits that can float. The most famous example is the coconut. Its seed is surrounded by a thick, fibrous layer that traps air, which makes it buoyant, and a hard shell that keeps seawater out. Coconuts can float for weeks or even months and still germinate when they wash up on a beach, which is partly why coconut palms are found on tropical coasts all over the world.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Third, animals. This is probably the most varied group. Many plants produce fruits that are brightly coloured and sweet, to attract birds and mammals. The animal eats the fruit, and the seeds pass through its digestive system unharmed and are deposited somewhere else, along with a useful supply of fertiliser. In some species, seeds actually germinate better after passing through an animal's gut. Other plants rely on animals in a less friendly way. Their seeds are covered in small hooks, which catch in fur or feathers, or in people's clothing. In fact, in the 1940s, a Swiss engineer called George de Mestral noticed how burdock seeds stuck to his dog's fur after a walk. He looked at them under a microscope, saw the tiny hooks, and used the idea to invent Velcro.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Animals that store food also help. Squirrels and jays, for example, bury acorns and other nuts to eat in winter. They don't find all of them again, and the forgotten ones can grow into new trees. It's been estimated that jays are responsible for planting a large proportion of the oak trees in some European woodlands.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Finally, self-dispersal, where the plant itself throws its seeds away. Some plants have seed pods that dry out and twist as they ripen, until they suddenly split open and fire the seeds into the air. Gorse, a spiny shrub common in Britain, is known for this, and on a hot summer day you can actually hear the pods cracking. Another example is Himalayan balsam, whose ripe pods burst open when they're touched, scattering seeds several metres. That has helped it to spread rapidly along riverbanks in Europe, where it's now considered an invasive species.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Understanding dispersal isn't just of academic interest. It helps us to predict how plants will respond as the climate changes and suitable areas shift. And when animals that disperse seeds decline, the plants that depend on them can decline as well. In the next session, we'll look at this in more detail, with a case study from tropical forests.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: I've looked at our notes from the classroom activity. You wrote that the group beside the window was more motivated, but I'm not sure we observed motivation directly. What exactly did we see that led you to that conclusion?

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: They started writing sooner and produced more ideas on their sheet. But you're right: that doesn't necessarily mean they were more motivated. They might have understood the instructions more quickly, or one member might have suggested an approach immediately.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia

dialogue.speaker: Evan

I'd like to record when each group begins the task, but we need to agree what 'begins' means. Talking about an idea might be part of the work even before anyone writes.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: For our exhibition, I originally thought we should show only the final models. They look much neater than the early attempts. But then visitors wouldn't see how our ideas developed, and that is the point of the assignment.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. We don't need every sketch, though. Let's choose one that shows a decision changing. Your first version had a handle at the top, and the later one moved it to the side. That would let us explain why trying the model affected the design.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: We should label the first model as a prototype, so nobody thinks it is a finished product. The caption needs to mention that it was made only to test the grip. We didn't test how long the material would last.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel

listening.title: Understanding a demonstration model

questions.prompt: The value of a demonstration depends on its __________.
questions.explanation: The model must have a defined explanatory purpose.
questions.evidenceQuote: Its usefulness depends on a clear purpose.

questions.evidenceQuote: an interesting visual change can be difficult to interpret

questions.prompt: An unexpected result may reveal a missing __________.

questions.evidenceQuote: they may reveal a missing assumption

questions.explanation: Limitations should be stated proactively.
questions.evidenceQuote: Its limitations should therefore appear in the explanation

groups.instruction: Questions 1–4. Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

listening.sourceNote: Original short skill drill. Not a complete IELTS test or an official past paper.
listening.contextDescription: A lecturer explains the purpose and limitations of a simplified model.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: A demonstration model represents selected features of a system. Its usefulness depends on a clear purpose. Imagine using a tray of sand to show how a channel changes when water flows through it. The model may make the movement of sediment visible, but that does not mean every detail behaves like a full-sized river. The scale, material and duration have all been changed.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Before beginning, state which relationship you want to demonstrate. Then identify which conditions will remain constant and which one you will vary. Otherwise, an interesting visual change can be difficult to interpret. If several things change together, you may not know which produced the result.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Keep a record of the sequence, including attempts that did not behave as expected. These are not automatically useless; they may reveal a missing assumption. However, an unexpected result should not immediately be treated as a discovery about the larger system. First check the model itself. A demonstration can generate a useful question without providing a complete answer. Its limitations should therefore appear in the explanation, rather than being mentioned only if someone challenges the conclusion.

listening.title: From a proposal to a reliable schedule

questions.prompt: A schedule shows relationships known as __________.
questions.explanation: Some activities depend on earlier tasks being completed.
questions.evidenceQuote: It also expresses dependencies.

questions.prompt: Consider people’s __________ as well as task duration.
questions.explanation: A qualified person may be occupied elsewhere.
questions.evidenceQuote: the availability of the people who carry it out

questions.prompt: Allow a __________ for minor delays.
questions.explanation: A buffer provides planned spare time.
questions.evidenceQuote: includes a buffer: a realistic allowance for minor delays

questions.prompt: Mark old schedule copies as __________.
questions.explanation: Clear version control prevents contradictory instructions.
questions.evidenceQuote: mark earlier copies as withdrawn

groups.instruction: Questions 1–4. Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

listening.sourceNote: Original short skill drill. Not a complete IELTS test or an official past paper.
listening.contextDescription: A lecturer discusses planning a small public event.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: A schedule is more than a list of activities with starting times. It also expresses dependencies. If a demonstration requires a table to be assembled first, the assembly is not simply another optional task. It must be completed before that activity can begin. Identifying these relationships early helps organisers see why a small delay in one place can affect several later events.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Distinguish the time an activity takes from the availability of the people who carry it out. A task requiring twenty minutes may still delay the programme for an hour if the only trained person is busy elsewhere. Recording responsibilities beside activities helps expose such conflicts before the event.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: A useful plan also includes a buffer: a realistic allowance for minor delays. This should not be confused with making every estimate deliberately vague. Explain what the extra time is intended to absorb. Finally, decide how changes will be communicated. A revised schedule helps only if the people affected receive it. Keeping several conflicting versions in circulation can create more confusion than the original delay. Use one clearly identified current version and mark earlier copies as withdrawn.

writing1.instructions: The diagram shows the stages in the production of chocolate from cocoa beans. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
processSteps: Ripe cocoa pods are harvested by hand from trees
Beans are removed and left to ferment for about a week
Fermented beans are dried in the sun
Dried beans are packed and shipped to factories
Beans are roasted at high temperature
Shells are removed and the beans are ground into a paste
Sugar and milk are mixed in and the mixture is refined
Liquid chocolate is poured into moulds and cooled
keyOverviewPoints: The process has eight stages, beginning on the farm and ending in the factory.
The first half takes place where the cocoa is grown; the second involves industrial processing.

writing1.title: Changes to a seaside village
writing1.instructions: The maps show the village of Portwell in 1980 and today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Portwell has changed from a fishing and farming village into a tourist resort.
Most farmland and the dunes have been replaced, though the beach remains.

writing1.title: Average house prices in three cities
writing1.instructions: The graph shows average house prices in three cities between 2010 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Prices rose overall in all three cities, most dramatically in Northport.
Southville fell at first before rising steeply after 2018.

writing1.title: Hours of sleep by age
writing1.instructions: The chart shows the average number of hours men and women in five age groups slept per night in one country. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Sleep fell from the youngest group to the middle-aged before recovering in older age.
Differences between men and women were small at every age.

writing1.title: Causes of food waste in homes
writing1.instructions: The pie chart shows the main reasons why food is thrown away in homes in one European country. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Food not being used in time is the leading cause, accounting for over a third.
Taste is the least common reason.

writing1.title: Museum visitors by month
writing1.instructions: The table shows the number of visitors to three museums in one city during four months of 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: The Science Museum was the most visited in every month.
July was the busiest month for all three, especially the Science Museum.

writing1.title: Recycling glass bottles
writing1.instructions: The diagram shows how glass bottles are recycled. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
processSteps: Used bottles are collected from homes and bottle banks
Bottles are taken to a recycling plant
Glass is sorted by colour and cleaned
Clean glass is crushed into small pieces called cullet
Cullet is melted in a furnace with sand and other materials
Molten glass is moulded into new bottles
New bottles are filled and sent to shops
keyOverviewPoints: Recycling glass is a cyclical process with seven stages.
It begins with collection and ends with new bottles returning to shops.

writing1.title: Redevelopment of a factory site
writing1.instructions: The maps show an old factory site and the plan for its redevelopment. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: The industrial site will become a residential area with community facilities.
The factory will be replaced by a park at the centre.

writing1.title: Rainfall and temperature in Darwin
writing1.instructions: The chart shows average monthly rainfall and temperature in the Australian city of Darwin. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Darwin has a very wet season and an almost completely dry season.
Temperatures stay warm all year, varying by only about five degrees.

writing1.title: Electric car sales
writing1.instructions: The graph shows electric cars as a percentage of new car sales in four countries from 2015 to 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Norway led throughout and electric cars became almost all new sales there.
China rose fastest after 2019, while Germany fell back after 2021.

writing1.title: Reasons for using public libraries
writing1.instructions: The chart shows the main reasons why adults and children used public libraries in one city in 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Borrowing books was the main reason for both groups.
Children used libraries more for social and study purposes; adults more for computers.

writing1.title: Sources of energy used in homes
writing1.instructions: The pie charts compare the sources of energy used for heating homes in one country in 1995 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Gas remained the main source but its share declined.
Heat pumps grew from a tiny share to the second largest, while oil almost disappeared.

writing1.title: Employment by sector
writing1.instructions: The table shows the percentage of workers employed in agriculture, industry and services in three countries in 1970 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Agriculture fell sharply in all three countries.
Services became the largest employer everywhere by 2020.

writing1.title: Producing olive oil
writing1.instructions: The diagram illustrates how olive oil is produced. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
processSteps: Olives are harvested from trees in autumn
Leaves and twigs are removed and the olives are washed
Olives are crushed into a paste, including the stones
The paste is slowly mixed for 30–40 minutes
The paste is spun in a centrifuge to separate oil from water and solids
Oil is left to settle in tanks
keyOverviewPoints: Olive oil production involves seven main stages.
Most of the process is mechanical and no heat is added.

writing1.title: Visitors to a national park
writing1.instructions: The graph shows the number of visitors to a national park by season between 2016 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Summer visitors far outnumbered winter visitors throughout.
Both seasons fell sharply in 2020 before recovering to record levels.

writing1.title: Water use per person
writing1.instructions: The chart shows average daily water use per person for four purposes in two cities. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: City A used much more water than City B, mainly because of gardens.
Bathing was the largest use in both cities.

writing1.title: Changes to a university campus
writing1.instructions: The maps show a university campus in 2000 and in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: The campus has become more developed, with new housing and research facilities.
The car park has been replaced, and public transport access improved.

writing1.title: Population and car ownership
writing1.instructions: The chart shows the population of a country and the number of cars per 1,000 people between 1980 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Car ownership rose much faster than population.
Population growth slowed after 2000, but car ownership kept increasing steadily.

writing1.title: Results of a survey on working hours
writing1.instructions: The table shows the results of a survey of employees in four industries about their weekly working hours. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: In every industry, the largest group worked 35–45 hours.
Retail had the most short-hours workers, finance the most long-hours workers.

writing1.title: Uses of mobile phones by teenagers
writing1.instructions: The pie chart shows how teenagers in one country spent their time on mobile phones in 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Social media and video together made up over 60% of phone time.
Schoolwork accounted for only a small fraction.

writing1.title: Average life expectancy in four countries
writing1.instructions: The graph shows average life expectancy at birth in four countries between 1960 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Life expectancy rose in all four countries.
Japan moved from second to highest; Nigeria remained lowest despite steady gains.

writing1.title: How people travel to work in three cities
writing1.instructions: The chart shows the main methods of travelling to work in three cities in 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Los Angeles relied overwhelmingly on cars, Tokyo on public transport and Copenhagen on bicycles.
Walking was a minor method everywhere.

writing1.title: Household waste composition
writing1.instructions: The pie charts show the composition of household waste in one city in 2000 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Plastic doubled its share, while paper fell sharply.
Food remained the largest category in both years.

writing1.title: Top international student destinations
writing1.instructions: The table shows the number of international students in five countries in 2005, 2015 and 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: The USA hosted the most students throughout.
Canada grew most dramatically, overtaking Australia by 2023.

writing1.title: How paper is recycled
writing1.instructions: The diagram shows the process of recycling paper. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
processSteps: Waste paper is collected from homes and offices
Paper is sorted by type and quality
Paper is mixed with water and chemicals to make pulp
Ink is removed by washing and air bubbles
Pulp is cleaned and screened to remove plastic and staples
Pulp is spread onto a mesh to drain water
Sheets are pressed and dried by heated rollers
New paper is cut into rolls and sent to customers
keyOverviewPoints: Recycling paper involves eight main stages.
The paper is turned into pulp, cleaned and then re-formed into new sheets.

writing1.title: How a hydroelectric dam produces electricity
writing1.instructions: The diagram shows how electricity is generated at a hydroelectric power station. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
processSteps: Rainwater fills a reservoir behind a dam
Gates open to let water flow into a large pipe
Water flows downhill and gains speed
The turbine drives a generator that produces electricity
Power lines carry electricity to homes and businesses
Water flows out into the river below the dam
keyOverviewPoints: Electricity is generated by the movement of water from a high reservoir to a lower river.
The process is continuous and does not burn fuel.

writing1.title: Changes to an airport
writing1.instructions: The maps show an airport in 2005 and how it looks today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: The airport has expanded significantly, with a second runway and a larger terminal.
Public transport links and new facilities have been added.

writing1.title: A town centre before and after pedestrianisation
writing1.instructions: The maps show a town centre in 1995 and today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: The centre has become pedestrian-friendly, with traffic removed from the main street.
Car-related facilities have been replaced by green space, housing and leisure uses.

writing1.title: Ice cream sales and temperature
writing1.instructions: The chart shows monthly ice cream sales and average temperature in one city over a year. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Ice cream sales closely followed temperature, peaking in July.
Sales were lowest in the coldest months.

writing1.title: Smartphone ownership by age
writing1.instructions: The graph shows the percentage of people in three age groups who owned a smartphone between 2010 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Ownership rose sharply in all age groups.
Young adults led throughout, while the oldest group grew most in later years, narrowing the gap.

writing1.title: Spending on leisure activities by income group
writing1.instructions: The chart shows average monthly spending on four leisure activities by low-, middle- and high-income households. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: High-income households spent far more on most activities, especially holidays.
Spending on streaming and games was similar across all groups.

writing1.title: Energy consumption per person
writing1.instructions: The table shows energy consumption per person in five countries in 1990 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
keyOverviewPoints: Canada had by far the highest consumption in both years.
China's consumption nearly quadrupled, while Germany's fell.

writing2.title: Health: individuals or governments
writing2.promptText: Some people think that individuals are responsible for their own health and should make better lifestyle choices. Others believe that governments should take more action to improve public health. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Eating less meat
writing2.promptText: In some countries, people are being encouraged to eat less meat for health and environmental reasons. Why do you think this is happening? Should governments try to influence what people eat?

writing2.title: Tourism and local people
writing2.promptText: Tourism is growing rapidly in many parts of the world. Do the advantages of tourism for local people outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Job security or flexibility
writing2.promptText: Some people prefer to work for one company for many years, while others prefer to change jobs frequently or work for themselves. Discuss the advantages of both approaches and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Social media and young people
writing2.promptText: Many young people now spend several hours a day on social media. What problems can this cause, and what measures could be taken to reduce these problems?

writing2.title: Memory in the digital age
writing2.promptText: Many people now rely on smartphones and the internet to remember information such as phone numbers, dates and facts. Why has this happened? Is this a positive or negative development?

writing2.title: Responding to extreme weather
writing2.promptText: Extreme weather events such as floods, droughts and heatwaves are becoming more common in many parts of the world. What problems does this cause, and what can governments and individuals do to reduce its effects?

writing2.title: Spending on roads or public transport
writing2.promptText: Some people think governments should spend money on building new roads, while others believe the money should be spent on improving public transport. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Fast food and health
writing2.promptText: Some people think that governments should tax fast food and sugary drinks to encourage people to eat more healthily. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Starting school early
writing2.promptText: In some countries, children start formal education at the age of four, while in others they start at seven. Do the advantages of starting school at an early age outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Old buildings or new?
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that old buildings should be preserved, while others think they should be replaced with modern buildings to meet the needs of growing cities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Private companies in space
writing2.promptText: Private companies are now playing a larger role in space exploration than governments did in the past. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: The plastic waste problem
writing2.promptText: The amount of plastic waste produced around the world is increasing rapidly. What problems does this cause, and what measures could be taken by governments, businesses and individuals to solve them?

writing2.title: Polluted rivers and lakes
writing2.promptText: In many parts of the world, rivers and lakes are becoming polluted. What are the main causes of this problem, and what can be done to solve it?

writing2.title: Pesticides and food prices
writing2.promptText: Some people think that governments should ban pesticides that harm insects, even if this makes food more expensive. Others believe that producing cheap food is more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Throwaway clothing
writing2.promptText: Many people now buy inexpensive clothes and throw them away after wearing them only a few times. What problems does this cause, and what measures could be taken to solve them?

writing2.title: Helping migrating animals
writing2.promptText: Many animals that migrate long distances, such as birds, fish and whales, are becoming less common. What problems do migrating animals face, and what can be done to help them?

writing2.title: Too many photographs?
writing2.promptText: Today, many people take hundreds of photographs with their phones every month but rarely look at them again. Why do people take so many photographs? Is this a positive or negative development?

writing2.title: Gardening at school
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that every school should have a garden and that all children should learn how to grow plants and food. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: University tuition
writing2.promptText: Some people think that university education should be free for all students, whatever their background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Practical vs academic subjects
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that schools should focus on practical skills such as managing money and cooking, while others think academic subjects are more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Online degrees
writing2.promptText: More and more students are choosing to study for a degree entirely online. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Falling interest in science
writing2.promptText: In many countries, fewer young people are choosing to study science at university. What are the reasons for this, and what can be done to encourage more students to study science?

writing2.title: Learning a foreign language
writing2.promptText: Many children now begin learning a foreign language at primary school. Why do you think this is happening? Is it a positive or negative development?

writing2.title: Homework
writing2.promptText: Some people argue that homework should be banned in primary schools because children need time to play. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Single-sex schools
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that boys and girls learn better in separate schools, while others think mixed schools are better. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Gap year
writing2.promptText: It is becoming common for young people to take a year off between finishing school and starting university. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Artificial intelligence and jobs
writing2.promptText: Some people fear that artificial intelligence will replace most human jobs within the next few decades. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

writing2.title: Screen time and children
writing2.promptText: Children today spend many hours every day using phones and computers. What problems does this cause, and what solutions can you suggest?

writing2.title: Cashless society
writing2.promptText: In many countries, people are using cash less and less, and paying for almost everything by card or phone. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Online friendships
writing2.promptText: Many people now have friends they have met only online. Why is this the case? Do you think online friendships can be as valuable as face-to-face friendships?

writing2.title: Privacy and security
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that governments should be allowed to monitor online communication to prevent crime, while others think this is a serious threat to privacy. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Space exploration
writing2.promptText: Some people think that the money spent on space exploration would be better spent on solving problems on Earth. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Driverless cars
writing2.promptText: In the future, most cars may drive themselves without human drivers. Do you think the advantages of this will outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Banning private cars in city centres
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that private cars should be banned from city centres. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Plastic waste
writing2.promptText: The amount of plastic waste produced worldwide is increasing rapidly. What are the main causes of this, and what measures could be taken to reduce it?

writing2.title: Individuals or governments
writing2.promptText: Some people say that individuals can do little to protect the environment and that only governments and large companies can make a difference. Others disagree. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Flying less
writing2.promptText: Air travel is one of the fastest-growing sources of greenhouse gas emissions. Should people be encouraged to fly less? How could this be achieved?

writing2.title: Vegetarian diets
writing2.promptText: More people are choosing to eat less meat or none at all. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Taxing fuel
writing2.promptText: The best way to reduce traffic and pollution is to make petrol much more expensive. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Water shortages
writing2.promptText: Many parts of the world are facing increasing shortages of fresh water. What are the causes of this problem, and what can be done to solve it?

writing2.title: Zoos
writing2.promptText: Some people think that zoos are cruel and should be closed, while others believe they play an important role in protecting wildlife. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Sugar tax
writing2.promptText: Governments should tax sugary drinks and unhealthy food in order to improve public health. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Rising obesity
writing2.promptText: Obesity rates among children are rising in many countries. What are the causes of this, and what can be done about it?

writing2.title: Mental health awareness
writing2.promptText: People today talk much more openly about mental health than in the past. Why has this change happened? Is it a positive development?

writing2.title: Free healthcare
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that healthcare should be completely free and paid for by the state, while others think people should pay for their own medical treatment. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Ageing population
writing2.promptText: In many countries, the proportion of older people is increasing. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages for society?

writing2.title: Sport in schools
writing2.promptText: Physical education should be a compulsory subject every day for all school students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Sleep deprivation
writing2.promptText: Many people today do not get enough sleep. Why is this, and what effects does it have on individuals and society?

writing2.title: Four-day working week
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that a four-day working week would be better for employees and employers. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Working from home
writing2.promptText: Since the pandemic, many companies allow employees to work from home for part or all of the week. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Job satisfaction or salary
writing2.promptText: Some people think that a high salary is the most important factor when choosing a job, while others believe job satisfaction matters more. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Changing careers
writing2.promptText: Nowadays many people change their career several times during their working lives. Why do you think this happens? Is it a positive or negative development?

writing2.title: Youth unemployment
writing2.promptText: In many countries, a large number of young people cannot find work after finishing their education. What are the causes, and what solutions can you suggest?

writing2.title: Retirement age
writing2.promptText: Governments should raise the retirement age because people are living longer. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Living in cities or the countryside
writing2.promptText: Some people prefer to live in big cities, while others prefer life in small towns or the countryside. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Housing costs
writing2.promptText: In many cities, the cost of housing has risen so much that young people cannot afford to buy a home. What are the causes of this, and what can be done?

writing2.title: Community service for young offenders
writing2.promptText: Young people who commit minor crimes should do unpaid work in the community instead of going to prison. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Family size
writing2.promptText: In many countries, families are much smaller than they were fifty years ago. What are the reasons for this? What effects does it have on society?

writing2.title: Living alone
writing2.promptText: An increasing number of people choose to live alone. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Celebrities as role models
writing2.promptText: Some people think that famous sports stars and entertainers are good role models for young people, while others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Volunteering
writing2.promptText: All young people should be required to do some unpaid voluntary work in their community. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Loneliness among the elderly
writing2.promptText: Many elderly people in modern societies feel lonely and isolated. What are the causes of this problem, and how could it be addressed?

writing2.title: Government funding for the arts
writing2.promptText: Governments should spend money on museums, theatres and art galleries rather than on sports facilities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Global culture
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that globalisation is making cultures around the world more similar, which is a loss. Others think it brings people closer together. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Reading books
writing2.promptText: Fewer people read books for pleasure than in the past. Why is this? What could be done to encourage reading?

writing2.title: Tourism in historic places
writing2.promptText: Large numbers of tourists now visit famous historic sites every year. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Preserving old buildings
writing2.promptText: Old buildings should always be protected, even if this prevents new development. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Disappearing languages
writing2.promptText: Many of the world's languages are disappearing. Why is this happening, and what can be done to protect them?

writing2.title: Advertising to children
writing2.promptText: Advertising aimed at children should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: News on social media
writing2.promptText: Some people think that social media is now the best source of news, while others believe traditional newspapers and television are more reliable. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Streaming services
writing2.promptText: People increasingly watch films and series on streaming platforms rather than at the cinema or on television. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Compulsory voting
writing2.promptText: Voting in elections should be compulsory for all adult citizens. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Public transport funding
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that public transport should be free and paid for by taxes, while others think passengers should pay the full cost. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Traffic congestion
writing2.promptText: Traffic congestion is becoming a serious problem in many large cities. What are the causes, and what measures could governments take to reduce it?

writing2.title: International aid
writing2.promptText: Rich countries often give financial aid to poorer countries. Why do they do this? Is financial aid the best way to help poorer nations?

writing2.title: Animal testing
writing2.promptText: Testing medicines on animals is necessary for medical progress and should continue. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Genetically modified crops
writing2.promptText: Some countries are growing more genetically modified crops to increase food production. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Funding research
writing2.promptText: Some people think that governments should fund scientific research that has practical benefits, while others believe pure research for its own sake is equally important. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Local food
writing2.promptText: People should buy food that is produced locally rather than food imported from other countries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Food waste
writing2.promptText: A large proportion of the food produced in the world is wasted. What are the causes of this, and what can be done to reduce it?

writing2.title: Leaving farming
writing2.promptText: In many countries, young people are leaving rural areas and fewer are choosing to work in farming. Why is this happening? What problems might it cause?

writing2.title: Shopping online
writing2.promptText: More and more people are doing their shopping online rather than in shops. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Corporate responsibility
writing2.promptText: Large companies have a responsibility to support the communities in which they operate, not just to make a profit. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Small shops and supermarkets
writing2.promptText: Some people think large supermarkets are good for consumers, while others believe they harm small local shops and communities. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Repair information
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that manufacturers should provide the parts and instructions needed to repair their products. Others think that repairs should only be carried out by the manufacturers themselves. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Choosing a timetable
writing2.promptText: Secondary school students should be allowed to choose when their school day begins and ends, provided that they attend all required lessons. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Shared facilities
writing2.promptText: Some new apartment buildings provide shared kitchens, workspaces and guest rooms instead of giving each household its own facilities. Do the advantages of this arrangement outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Missed connections
writing2.promptText: Passengers sometimes avoid using public transport because they cannot rely on connections between services. What problems does this cause, and what could transport operators do to address them?

writing2.title: Recording family histories
writing2.promptText: Some people record interviews with older relatives to preserve their family histories. Why might they choose to do this? Should schools encourage students to take part in such projects?

writing2.title: Publishing salaries
writing2.promptText: Some people think that employers should make the salaries of all employees available to their colleagues. Others believe that this information should remain private. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Packaging responsibility
writing2.promptText: Shops should be required to take back the packaging of the products they sell. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Visitor reservations
writing2.promptText: Some popular tourist attractions require visitors to book a particular arrival time rather than allowing them to arrive whenever they wish. Do the advantages of this policy outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Empty meeting spaces
writing2.promptText: In some neighbourhoods, public meeting rooms remain unused even though residents say they need places to meet. Why might this happen, and what could be done to make better use of these rooms?

writing2.title: Automatic recommendations
writing2.promptText: Online services can recommend music, films and books based on what a person has previously chosen. How might these recommendations affect the choices people make? Is this a positive or negative development?

writing2.title: Local projects at university
writing2.promptText: Some people believe university students should complete a project that benefits the local community before graduating. Others think their time should be devoted entirely to academic study. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Paid trial work
writing2.promptText: Employers should be required to pay job applicants for any trial work they ask them to perform. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Borrowing household equipment
writing2.promptText: Some communities operate services through which residents can borrow tools and household equipment instead of buying them. Do the advantages of these services outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Complicated application forms
writing2.promptText: People can find it difficult to apply for public services because the forms and instructions are complicated. What effects can this have, and how could public authorities improve the application process?

writing2.title: Temporary exhibitions
writing2.promptText: Some museums organise temporary exhibitions that remain open for only a few weeks. Why might museums choose to do this? Should they focus more on their permanent collections?

writing2.title: School streets
writing2.promptText: Some people believe roads beside schools should be closed to cars at the beginning and end of the school day. Others think these restrictions create difficulties for local residents. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Subscription cancellation
writing2.promptText: Cancelling a subscription to a service should be as easy as signing up for it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Rotating team leadership
writing2.promptText: In some workplaces, team members take turns leading a project rather than having one permanent team leader. Do the advantages of this approach outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Unused teacher feedback
writing2.promptText: Some students read the marks on their assignments but pay little attention to their teachers' written feedback. Why might this happen, and what could teachers and students do to make feedback more useful?

writing2.title: Naming public places
writing2.promptText: Local authorities sometimes invite residents to suggest names for new streets and public buildings. What benefits might this bring? Should residents or elected officials make the final decision?

writing2.title: Exams and assessment
writing2.promptText: Some people believe that exams are not a good way to assess students and that continuous assessment through coursework is fairer. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Teachers or technology
writing2.promptText: Some people think that computers and the internet will eventually replace teachers in the classroom. Others believe teachers will always be essential. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: University dropout
writing2.promptText: In many countries, a significant number of students leave university before completing their degree. What are the reasons for this, and what can be done to help students complete their studies?

writing2.title: Studying abroad
writing2.promptText: An increasing number of students choose to study in a foreign country. What are the reasons for this trend? Is it a positive development for the students' home countries?

writing2.title: Learning at home
writing2.promptText: Some parents choose to educate their children at home rather than send them to school. Do the advantages of home schooling outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Robots caring for the elderly
writing2.promptText: In the future, robots may be used to look after elderly people in their homes. Some people think this is a good idea. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Fake news
writing2.promptText: False information spreads quickly on the internet and social media. What problems does this cause, and what can be done to tackle it?

writing2.title: Children and smartphones
writing2.promptText: Some people think children should not be allowed smartphones until they are teenagers, while others believe phones help children stay safe and learn. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Video games
writing2.promptText: Video games are now one of the most popular forms of entertainment in the world. Why are they so popular? Do they have a positive or negative effect on young people?

writing2.title: Facial recognition
writing2.promptText: Police in some cities now use facial recognition cameras in public places. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Tourism and the environment
writing2.promptText: International tourism is harmful to the environment and should be limited. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Air pollution in cities
writing2.promptText: Air pollution is a serious problem in many large cities. What are the main causes, and what measures could be taken to improve air quality?

writing2.title: Nuclear power
writing2.promptText: Some people believe nuclear power is the best way to reduce carbon emissions, while others think it is too dangerous and expensive. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Fast fashion
writing2.promptText: Many people buy cheap clothes and throw them away after wearing them only a few times. Why do people do this? What can be done to reduce the environmental impact?

writing2.title: Electric cars
writing2.promptText: Many governments are encouraging people to switch to electric cars. Do the advantages of this policy outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Banning smoking completely
writing2.promptText: Smoking should be made completely illegal. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Alternative medicine
writing2.promptText: Some people prefer traditional or alternative medicine to modern medical treatment. Others think only scientifically tested treatments should be used. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Stress at work
writing2.promptText: Many workers today suffer from stress. What are the causes of this, and how can employers and employees reduce it?

writing2.title: Life expectancy
writing2.promptText: People are living longer than ever before. What are the reasons for this? What challenges does it create for society?

writing2.title: Equal pay
writing2.promptText: Governments should make it a legal requirement for companies to publish what they pay all their employees. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Working for a large or small company
writing2.promptText: Some people prefer to work for large international companies, while others prefer small local businesses. Discuss the advantages of both and give your own opinion.

writing2.title: Skills shortages
writing2.promptText: Many industries report that they cannot find workers with the right skills. Why is this happening, and what can be done about it?

writing2.title: Automation in factories
writing2.promptText: Robots and machines are replacing many factory workers. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Public spending on the elderly
writing2.promptText: Governments should spend more money on services for older people than on services for young people. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Crime prevention
writing2.promptText: Some people think the best way to reduce crime is longer prison sentences, while others believe education and job training are more effective. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Moving to cities
writing2.promptText: Many people around the world are moving from rural areas to cities. Why is this happening? What problems does it cause?

writing2.title: Living in a multicultural society
writing2.promptText: Many cities today are home to people from many different cultures. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Learning history
writing2.promptText: History is one of the most important subjects at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Traditional or modern architecture
writing2.promptText: Some people think new buildings should follow traditional local styles, while others prefer modern designs. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Loss of traditional skills
writing2.promptText: Traditional skills such as handicrafts and local cooking are disappearing in many countries. Why is this happening, and what can be done to preserve them?

writing2.title: Celebrity news
writing2.promptText: Newspapers and websites give too much attention to the private lives of celebrities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Podcasts and radio
writing2.promptText: Podcasts have become very popular in recent years. Why do you think this is? Will they replace traditional radio?

writing2.title: Free public transport
writing2.promptText: Public transport in cities should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: National service
writing2.promptText: Some people believe all young people should do a year of national service, either military or community work. Others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

writing2.title: Antibiotic resistance
writing2.promptText: Many antibiotics are becoming less effective because bacteria are developing resistance. Why is this happening, and what can be done?

writing2.title: Organic food
writing2.promptText: Organic food is a luxury that most families cannot afford, and governments should not encourage it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Urban farming
writing2.promptText: In some cities, people are growing food on rooftops and in community gardens. Why is this becoming popular? Can urban farming make a real contribution to food supplies?

writing2.title: Advertising in schools
writing2.promptText: Some schools accept money from companies in exchange for displaying advertisements. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

writing2.title: Shopping on Sundays
writing2.promptText: Shops should be closed on one day each week so that workers can rest. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

writing2.title: Global brands
writing2.promptText: Some people think global brands bring better products to consumers, while others believe they damage local businesses and culture. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
